What a /12 means

A /12 holds 1,048,576 addresses. Blocks this size are regional or provider aggregates and are always subdivided before use.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /12 uses 12 network bits and leaves 20 host bits, so the block contains 1,048,576 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−12) − 2 = 1,048,576 − 2 = 1,048,574.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.240.0.0
!
access-list 10 permit 10.0.0.0 0.15.255.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.0.1/12

Linux

ip addr add 10.0.0.1/12 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /12?

1,048,574. A /12 has 1,048,576 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 1,048,574 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /12?

255.240.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.15.255.255.
